**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

I suspect your issue is on the reflection side as you are likely getting back an Integer datatype for your boolean column. However even in that case, I can't reproduce any problem.

next would be to try a self-contained cx_Oracle test which we can show to Anthony on his github, but in the meantime here's my self-contained repro, if you want to see if you get the same result here:


```
import sqlalchemy as sa
import sqlalchemy.orm
import datetime
import sqlalchemy.ext.declarative

connection_string = "oracle://scott:tiger@oracle1120/"

engine = sa.create_engine(connection_string, echo = True, max_overflow = 0, pool_size = 3)
_session = sa.orm.sessionmaker()
_session.configure(bind=engine)
session = _session()

table = sa.Table(
    "pod_test", sa.MetaData(),
    sa.Column("id", sa.Integer, primary_key=True),
    sa.Column("converge", sa.Boolean),
    sa.Column("sat", sa.String(50)),
    sa.Column("stime_utc", sa.DateTime),
    sa.Column("etime_utc", sa.DateTime)
)
table.drop(engine)
table.create(engine, checkfirst=True)


Base = sa.ext.declarative.declarative_base()


class Pod(Base):
    __table__ = sa.Table(
        "pod_test", Base.metadata, autoload = True, autoload_with = engine)

session.add(Pod(id=1, converge=True, sat="M02"))
session.commit()

# Create new object

nap = Pod()

nap.id = 1
nap.sat = "M03"
nap.stime_utc = datetime.datetime(2018, 5, 14, 18, 5, 42)
nap.etime_utc = datetime.datetime(2018, 5, 14, 18, 10, 42)
nap.converge = False

session.merge(nap)

# Commit session

session.commit()


```

Here's a standalone cx_Oracle script.  Can you try this?   This also works for me, that is, directly passing True/False to an integer column.  If this fails for you then we can go over to cx_Oracle's github and figure out what's going on.  I just don't know how the presence of instantclient affects anything b.c. I run cx_Oracle here without any dependencies.

```
import cx_Oracle

c = cx_Oracle.connect(
    dsn=cx_Oracle.makedsn("oracle1120", 1521), user="scott", password="tiger")

cursor = c.cursor()

try:
    cursor.execute("drop table foo")
except:
    pass

cursor.execute("""
    create table foo(
        id integer primary key,
        data SMALLINT
    )
""")

cursor.execute("INSERT INTO foo (id, data) VALUES (:id, :data)", {"id": 1, "data": True})
cursor.execute("UPDATE foo SET data=:data", {"data": False})
```

**Leonid Butenko wrote:**

Yes, the version of instantclient changes the result. But please pay attention, that the version of sqlalchemy changes the result as well. If I use 1.1.13 - everything works in all versions of instantclient.

```
# python test_michael2.py 
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test_michael2.py", line 20, in <module>
    cursor.execute("INSERT INTO foo (id, data) VALUES (:id, :data)", {"id": 1, "data": True})
cx_Oracle.DatabaseError: ORA-03115: unsupported network datatype or representation
```

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

It's not surprising that the result changes as of SQLAlchemy 1.2; please see http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_12.html#major-refactor-to-cx-oracle-dialect-typing-system which details how the cx_Oracle dialect was almost entirely rewriten to use cx_Oracle 6.x properly.    The issue here is likely that SQLAlchemy 1.2 is no longer calling upon setinputsizes() for numeric types, [per the advice of Anthony Tuininga](https://github.com/oracle/python-cx_Oracle/issues/68#issuecomment-323467079). That is, if you try the script like this, it probably works (it would help if you could confirm):

```
cursor.setinputsizes(id=cx_Oracle.NUMBER, data=cx_Oracle.NUMBER)
cursor.execute("INSERT INTO foo (id, data) VALUES (:id, :data)", {"id": 1, "data": True})
cursor.setinputsizes(data=cx_Oracle.NUMBER)
cursor.execute("UPDATE foo SET data=:data", {"data": False})
```

The reason for instantclient affecting the behavior here needs to be understood since this may be evidence of a bug in cx_Oracle or instantclient, or at least suggest the best place for it to be worked around.    It seems that cx_Oracle at the very least should be able to coerce True/False into integers if that's what's needed.    I've posted at https://github.com/oracle/python-cx_Oracle/issues/181 .

In the meantime, the canonical way to make use of SQLAlchemy's Boolean type with reflection is that you have to specify it explicitly:


```
class Pod(Base):
    __table__ = sa.Table(
        "pod_test", Base.metadata,
        sa.Column("converge", sa.Boolean),
        autoload = True, autoload_with = engine)

```

this is documented at http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/core/reflection.html#overriding-reflected-columns.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

per Anthony if you are running Oracle 11g you should be on the 11.x instantclient series too.  "known issue" per him (though I don't have a link)

**Leonid Butenko wrote:**

Yes, indeed, i confirm that calling 

```
cursor.setinputsizes(data=cx_Oracle.NUMBER)
```
prior to every cursor.execute from previous test eliminates the problem.

Thanks for submitting an issue to the cx_oracle support. I'm still confused though. If you open the cx_oracle website it cleraly states:


```
cx_Oracle 6 has been tested with Python version 2.7, and with versions 3.4 and higher. 
You can use cx_Oracle with Oracle 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2 client libraries. Oracle's standard 
client-server version interoperability allows connection to both older and newer 
databases. For example Oracle 12.2 client libraries can connect to Oracle Database 11.2.
```
So following Anthony's advice I will try to downgrade the version of instantclient to 11.2 in our system. It looks like the only reasonable solution, that doesn't require a code modification from our side and at the same time using the most recent versions of other software like sqlalchemy and cx_oracle.

Thanks btw for the rapid response and helpful advises! It has really saved me a lot of time!

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

I may have misinterpreted on the 11G side of things.  The issue is that I don't want to setinputsizes() for all integers, but also I don't want to scan all numbers for their being True/False so seeing if a cx_Oracle inputtypehandler can intercept these more specifically.

**Leonid Butenko wrote:**

Well, if I have correctly understood the root of the problem, there should be a clean solution for the future. One or another (sqlalchemy or cx_Oracle) should somehow sort it out. If you decide not to wrap booleans in sqlalchemy (what I kind of understand and agree), then we might try to force Anthony to do it more accurately in cx_Oracle and/or at least document it for others.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

the problem is that for the current "setinputsizes" logic I have, I can only say, "call setinputsizes for all cx_Oracle.NUMBER", and that is too broad.   I would need to alter the auto-setinputsizes thing to only happen for integers.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

I have an approach in review at https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/#/q/Ida80cc2c2c37ffc0e05da4b5df2dadfab55a01f2.

can you try the patch at https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/changes/757/revisions/d494e338842bd59ccbc446c03f2cf54df9896bcd/patch?zip  (or otherwise download style of your choice at https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/#/c/zzzeek/sqlalchemy/+/757/ in the upper right corner) and confirm this fixes your issue?  thanks

**Leonid Butenko wrote:**

Michael, I have compiled the new version of sqlalchemy and installed it into my docker container from above.  I ran the example from your first post and can confirm it's working fine with cx_oracle 6.3 and instantclient 12.2.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

call setinputsizes() for integer types

Altered the Oracle dialect such that when an :class:`.Integer` type is in
use, the cx_Oracle.NUMERIC type is set up for setinputsizes().  In
SQLAlchemy 1.1 and earlier, cx_Oracle.NUMERIC was passed for all numeric
types unconditionally, and in 1.2 this was removed to allow for better
numeric precision.  However, for integers, some database/client setups
will fail to coerce boolean values True/False into integers which introduces
regressive behavior when using SQLAlchemy 1.2.  Overall, the setinputsizes
logic seems like it will need a lot more flexibility going forward so this
is a start for that.

Change-Id: Ida80cc2c2c37ffc0e05da4b5df2dadfab55a01f2
Fixes: #4259

**Migrated issue, originally created by Leonid Butenko**

Hi,

I think it might be somehow related to the #4259, but with floats now.

I use Oracle 11g, cx_oracle 6.3, oracle_instantclient 11.2 and sqlalchemy 1.2.7

here is my test program
```
import sqlalchemy as sa
import sqlalchemy.orm
import datetime
import sqlalchemy.ext.declarative

connection_string = "oracle://scott:tiger@oracle1120/"

engine = sa.create_engine(connection_string, echo = True, max_overflow = 0, pool_size = 3)
_session = sa.orm.sessionmaker()
_session.configure(bind=engine)
session = _session()

table = sa.Table(
    "nan_test", sa.MetaData(),
    sa.Column("id", sa.Integer, primary_key=True),
    sa.Column("fval", sa.Float)
)
table.drop(engine)
table.create(engine, checkfirst=True)

Base = sa.ext.declarative.declarative_base()

class Pod(Base):
    __table__ = sa.Table(
        "nan_test", Base.metadata, autoload = True, autoload_with = engine)

session.add(Pod(id=1, fval=float('nan')))
session.commit()
```

I'm not sure whether it is the correct place to report about this problem. It might be cx_oracle related issue. From my point of view, passing NaNs to floating columns should be a normal practice at least in the scientific world, so I thought sqlalchemy might handle this situation as well. Pls advise! 

The solution I found so far is to downgrade the version of cx_oracle to 6.0.1 or ealier.
```
>  conda install cx_oracle=6.0b2

The following packages will be DOWNGRADED:

    cx_oracle: 6.0.3-py27hc82e58e_0 --> 6.0b2-py27_0
> python test.py
....
```
